label: MORNING BRIEF

stories.title: Heirs of occupants win new rights
stories.story: The Supreme Court ruled on 13 Nov that heirs can rely on a late parent’s years on registered land to claim bona fide occupancy, if the parent had been there 12 years.
stories.you: Families on a titled plot may have rights. Ask how long they’ve been there before you list it.

stories.title: Equity says the Dei auction goes ahead
stories.story: Equity Bank says no court order stops the sale of Magoola’s company properties to recover over Shs148 billion. They include homes in Muyenga, Kitende and Seguku.
stories.you: Clients may be tempted. Get a lawyer’s opinion before anyone bids on a disputed sale.

stories.title: Shs3.5bn payout goes missing
stories.story: The Muslim Supreme Council says Shs3.5 billion paid by government for its land was withdrawn on 81 cheques. Former directors are still the registered owners.
stories.you: Selling for a mosque, church or company? Check who signs — and whose name is on the title.

stories.title: Kampala–Jinja train from December
stories.story: Passenger trains between Kampala and Jinja are set to start in December 2026. The working network is to grow from 269 km to about 650 km by year end.
stories.you: Commuters will look along the line. Mention the train in listings near a station.
stories.source: Sources: Uganda Update News, Daily Monitor · 15 Nov 2026

stories.title: Power may run short by 2030
stories.story: The Energy Ministry warns of a shortfall of almost one gigawatt by 2030 unless investment speeds up. Demand is growing 15% a year.
stories.you: Buyers will ask about power. Solar and backup power make a listing stand out.
